review_comments.body:
[P1] Content filtering can still be incorrectly reported as a tool call.

In common.go:385-386, this PR adds a mapping from content_filter to refusal. However, chatStopReason in the same file only explicitly protects max_tokens.

If the response also contains tool_calls, the function will override refusal and return tool_use instead.

This affects both non-streaming and streaming paths, as they both use this function. If the upstream provider has already emitted tool calls before triggering content filtering, the client may proceed with tool execution while the actual refusal result is hidden.

Recommendation: Give refusal the same precedence as max_tokens over tool_use, and add regression tests covering this combination in both streaming and non-streaming paths.

comments.body:
Good catch, thanks. `chatStopReason` now gives `refusal` the same precedence as `max_tokens` over `tool_use`, so a response that emitted tool calls and then hit the content filter reports `refusal`. Added regression tests for the combination in both paths: a `content_filter` case in `TestChatResponseToMessagesResponseStopReasonFromContent` (non-streaming) and `TestToChatStreamContentFilterWinsOverToolCalls` (streaming). Both fail before the change and pass with it.

This change was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent (Claude Code).
